chapter: Postwar Chicago, Janis and De Paris
title: Chicago blues and a working drummer's routine
summary: He did not get to know the rhythm-and-blues drummers because of his work schedule.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: At that time in Chicago, there was an interest in, let's say, Blues. Chicago has always been a Blues town. But there were musicians who were playing with, say, kind of
a Jazz-like heavy backbeat and so forth. Did you get a chance to talk with any of those drummers who played that... It was a Rhythm-and-Blues, a type of Rhythm-and-Blues.

No, I didn't get a chance to talk with many of them. I was always going out to work. I worked so hard! So I might get up at about eleven o'clock and get me something to eat, and come right back and get into bed again. Because that was a hard job. I had to keep all my health and strength together. I always had... All the bandleaders and everybody I worked with always said I had a good foot, you know, a good ride foot.
